newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania July inflation seen down, below two pct.
newsitem.headline: Romania July inflation seen down, below two pct.

text.p: Romania's July inflation is expected to drop below two percent, its lowest rate this year, from 2.3 percent last month, the government said on Tuesday.
A government statement said Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea announced the figures in a meeting with trade unions.

Monthly inflation hit a peak of more than 30 percent in March. That was after Ciorbea's government began liberalising prices as part of market reforms introduced in November, when it defeated ex-communists in elections.

Inflation has since receded, but initial targets of year-on-year 90-percent inflation for 1997 have stillbeen revised up. Ministers have revised their forecasts to 110 percent, but analysts said they expected final figures closer to 150 percent.

Ciorbea made his announcement during the International Monetary Fund's mission to Romania to gauge whether the country has met requirements for the second of five disbursements each for an $86 million standby credit.

The mission, due to remain in Bucharest until next week, has yet to comment on the government's programme in reducing inflation, proceeding with stalled privatisation and closing down inefficient farms and industries.
